title: How much Net Income for each $100 of Revenue?
introduction: Start with the two figures Apple reported, then put their relationship on one simple scale.

discovery.heading: Notice
discovery.prompt: Revenue is much larger. How can we compare their relationship on one simple scale?
discovery.support: Next, FinPath will put Revenue on a $100 comparison scale.
discovery.revealLabel: Compare them on a $100 Revenue scale

ratioBoundary: This is a comparison ratio. It does not mean this amount of cash moved, was generated, or was retained.
terminology: Net Profit Margin uses Net Income. It is not Apple’s ‘Gross margin’ dollar subtotal from the previous lesson.

question.prompt: If Revenue were $100 and the margin stayed the same, about how much would be Net Income?
question.hint: Choose one. This is practice, not a score.
question.supportedFeedback: That uses the Net Profit Margin as the Net Income share of a $100 Revenue scale.
question.unsupportedFeedback: That is the remainder of the $100 comparison scale, not the Net Income share. It is not one Apple-reported expense line.

verification.unitNote: Apple reports USD millions. FinPath displays the same reported values in USD billions before deriving the ratio.
verification.roundingNote: FinPath calculates with the exact reported values, verifies to three decimal places, and displays the learning result to one decimal place.

limitation: Net Profit Margin alone does not explain why the margin changed, how much cash Apple generated, whether Apple’s shares are fairly priced, or whether Apple is a good investment.

sources.title: Beginners’ Guide to Financial Statements
supports: Revenue and Net Income teaching context
